classification_append.prior_dependency: docs/RESOURCE_ITEM_OWNERSHIP.md and reports/resource_item_ownership_audit.json establish the outer fast-path appends and non-releasing list teardown; unchanged by this packet.
classification_append.valid_domain: Well-formed four-byte pointer-range list with begin/end/end-capacity ordered and aligned; normal append sets position=end and count1; value-address readable. Allocation and CRT copy success are required.
classification_append.ownership: Both outer fast path and normal slow growth append copy pointer values only. None of the verified item-copy/fill operations accesses the pointed item, increments its reference count, releases it, or invokes a pointee method. Derived lists therefore borrow the items under the verified normal append/destruction route.
classification_append.values: Existing order and duplicate pointer values are preserved. Null pointer VALUES are copied unchanged by helpers, though outer concrete classifier0071bb40 skips null items. There is no deduplication, item identity check or reference transfer in these helpers. A null value-ADDRESS is invalid; it is dereferenced before checking insertion count.
classification_append.growth: old size=end-begin divided by4, capacity=end-cap-begin divided by4, treating null begin as size/capacity0. Reject required size above3FFFFFFFh through existing typed xlen throw helper. Candidate capacity=old capacity+floor(old capacity/2), replaced by0 when it exceeds maximum, then clamped up to required. Normal empty first allocation has capacity1.
classification_append.order: Snapshot value into stack argument storage before any allocation, preserving an input value-address that aliases the old backing array. Allocate by capacity, copy [old begin,position), fill count raw values, copy [position,old end), then free old nonnull backing and commit new begin/end/end-capacity. For append, suffix length0.
classification_append.external: Allocation helpers00714120/00714180/007141e0 receive ECX capacity and EDX0; internals remain external. Generic middle/multiple-insert non-growth branches are matched but their helper contracts and malformed-input behavior are not reconstructed.

node_layout.mapped_value_slot: 14h (not read or destroyed by matched erase body)

cache_erase.lookup: Lower-bound plus reverse less-than rejects greater candidates, so only an equivalent key is erased. Empty markers compare by length0; nonempty strings compare through CRTstricmp. Length is an emptiness marker, not a byte bound for comparison. Queries and nodes require valid native-string pair storage and valid nonempty C strings.
cache_erase.duplicates_and_identity: Callback attempts one iterator erasure and returns; no loop removes a key range. If equivalent duplicate keys exist outside the assumed map invariant, only the found node is targeted. No expected resource pointer or mapped-value equality check exists: removal is solely by the current name key. Cache insertion uniqueness remains external.
cache_erase.missing_and_null: Missing key resolves to sentinel and is a no-op. Length0 keys can use null data because their data is not read for comparison. Null name-pair pointer, null candidate storage, or nonempty strings with null data lie outside valid input. No null mapped-value guard is required because the mapped value is not read by the matched erase body.
cache_erase.node_lifetime: Normal iterator erase relinks a node with zero/one children directly; the two-child branch relinks the successor node and swaps colors instead of copying key/mapped-value payload. Then it performs red-black repair through structural helpers, tears down the original erased key buffer, frees the original erased node, conditionally decrements nonzero tree count, and writes successor owner/node to output iterator.
cache_erase.mapped_lifetime: The erased-node cleanup explicitly operates on key length/data then node allocation, without reading mapped slot+14, item AddRef/Release, InterlockedDecrement or virtual item dispatch. This is a non-releasing name removal at the matched function-body boundary. It does not independently prove every cache insertion is non-retaining; insertion is not audited here. Structural successor/min/max/rotation helper internals remain external.
cache_erase.name_correction: Old nameSTL_xlen_throw_00b7fa60 mistakes an invalid-iterator exception branch for the whole function. Full716-byte body has normal RB-tree erase and RET12. Suggested correctionBSP_ResourceNameTree_EraseIterator; worker did not rename.

ghidra_findings.alias_warning: Pseudocode discarded the real00b7fb6c..00b7fbc1 two-child replacement branch as unreachable. Assembly passes ECX=&stack iterator to00b7ce80, reloads its node at00b7fafe, and branches to that region. This is consistent with missing decompiler knowledge of successor-helper stack-iterator mutation; that cause is an inference and the callee internals remain external. The audit follows full matched machine code.
